selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What did the traveller do when he wanted to learn about the World of the Unseen?
questions.answer: He carefully examined it and approached it with both his mind and heart, asking what it reveals.

questions.question: According to the passage, what do the crafted things in the visible world say about their Maker’s intention?
questions.answer: They show that their Maker intends to introduce Himself to His creatures.

questions.question: Why did the traveller conclude that this Being would also speak?
questions.answer: Because One who makes Himself known by actions would also make Himself known by speech.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the first way Allah makes Himself known?
questions.answer: Through deeds, creation, and the natural language of things.

questions.question: How is the witness of revelation described when compared with the witness of the universe?
questions.answer: It is described as even stronger.

questions.question: Why is revelation a greater proof than the universe alone?
questions.answer: Because it comes from Allah directly and gives a clearer witness to His existence and oneness.

questions.question: Besides making Allah known, what else does His speech reveal?
questions.answer: It also shows His attributes.

questions.question: What double function does divine speech have in the passage?
questions.answer: It makes Allah known and also makes His attributes known.

questions.question: How many sacred truths does the traveller understand revelation declares at this point?
questions.answer: Five sacred truths.

questions.question: What number of core truths did the traveller understand revelation proclaims?
questions.answer: He understood that it proclaims five.

questions.question: What question was in the traveller’s mind as he turned toward the unseen world?
questions.answer: He wanted to know what message that world gives.

questions.question: What did he infer from the beauty and skill seen in the physical world?
questions.answer: He inferred that there is a Maker behind it who wants to be known.

questions.question: What do the many skillful works point to besides power?
questions.answer: They point to hidden perfection and wisdom.

questions.question: What is meant by making Himself known through the “tongue of disposition”?
questions.answer: It means creation itself, by the way it exists and functions, points to Him without spoken language.

questions.question: After entering the unseen world with his heart, what major truth does he notice first?
questions.answer: He notices that revelation is strongly present across the unseen world.

questions.question: What was the first major reality he saw in that realm?
questions.answer: He saw that revelation has a powerful and ongoing presence in it.

questions.question: How is Allah’s speech described in relation to His knowledge and power?
questions.answer: It is from the One whose knowledge and power are present everywhere.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Allah’s own speech?
questions.answer: It teaches that His speech is eternal, fitting for Him, and endless.

questions.question: What in the revealed books helps confirm revelation?
questions.answer: Their signs, proofs, and miracles help confirm it.

questions.question: What proof inside the scriptures is mentioned?
questions.answer: Their miracles and evidences are mentioned.

questions.question: Which two inner abilities did the traveller use to explore the unseen world?
questions.answer: He used his intellect and his heart.

questions.question: What was he hoping to learn by doing that?
questions.answer: He was hoping to learn what the unseen world testifies to and teaches.

questions.question: What do the many extraordinary works reveal about their Maker?
questions.answer: They reveal His hidden excellence and perfect qualities.

questions.question: What image does the passage use for the traveller’s effort to learn from the unseen world?
questions.answer: It describes him as knocking at its door.
